messages:
maria: Quick Helm question — trying to conditionally mount either a projected serviceAccountToken or a k8s Secret into a sidecar depending on k8s version and a chart value. When the secret is not present the template errors with a nil pointer during `helm template` in CI. Anyone seen a clean pattern for this?

maria: minimal snippet I'm using right now (simplified):
```yaml
volumes:
  - name: sa-token
    projected:
      sources:
        - serviceAccountToken:
            path: token
            expirationSeconds: 86400
```
and when using a Secret instead:
```yaml
volumes:
  - name: sa-token
    secret:
      secretName: {{ .Values.sidecar.secret.name }}
```
The problem is I want to render the `secret:` block only if `.Values.sidecar.secret.name` is set, otherwise render the `projected:` block. Doing `if` around the inner fields still errors in some combos.

ryan: For `helm template` the usual safe approach is to guard the entire volume entry, not just the inner keys. Helm will still try to evaluate some expressions if the object structure is present. Example pattern:
```gotmpl
{{- if .Values.sidecar.secret.name }}
- name: sa-token
  secret:
    secretName: {{ .Values.sidecar.secret.name | quote }}
{{- else }}
- name: sa-token
  projected:
    sources:
      - serviceAccountToken:
          path: token
          expirationSeconds: 86400
{{- end }}
```
That moves the branching to the top-level element so Helm doesn't try to access `.Values.sidecar.secret.name` when it's empty.

ryan: If you need to detect an existing cluster Secret at render time (e.g., for installs vs CI `helm template`), `lookup` can be used but it requires cluster access, so CI `helm template` will still fail to see it. Eg: `{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace .Values.sidecar.secret.name }}` and then `if $s` — but again only works when rendering against a cluster.

maria: Ah right, we're running `helm template` in CI without cluster. So `lookup` is out. I tried putting `required` around the value but that fails the whole render if absent which we don't want.

jeff: Another trick is to allow configuring a `mode` in values: .Values.sidecar.tokenSource: "projected" | "secret". The chart then trusts the values to decide rendering instead of probing the cluster. Less magic, more explicit.

maria: Yea we added `sidecar.tokenSource` in the values and default to `projected`. Updated snippet: 
```gotmpl
{{- if eq .Values.sidecar.tokenSource "secret" }}
- name: sa-token
  secret:
    secretName: {{ .Values.sidecar.secret.name | quote }}
{{- else }}
- name: sa-token
  projected:
    sources:
      - serviceAccountToken:
          path: token
          expirationSeconds: 86400
{{- end }}
```
This rendered fine in CI.

ryan: Also worth adding a validation in `values.schema.json` (if you use it) so people can't set `tokenSource: secret` without providing `sidecar.secret.name`. Give a helpful error message during `helm lint`.

jeff: Can you drop the PR here when ready? I can glance for other chart patterns we want to keep consistent.

maria: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/412 — includes `values.schema.json` change + unit test for `helm template`.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: staging chart lint + template check passed for PR #412 :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks all :heart: this unblocked our staging test.
